summary: History of North Korea's Kim dynasty, from Kim Il Sung's Soviet-backed rise and Kim Jong Il's famine-era rule to Kim Jong Un, raised in isolated luxury and Swiss schools, who took power in 2011 and expanded purges and nuclear weapons.

evidence.note: Kim Il Sung's 1912 birth and guerrilla career open the family history
Kim Il Sung trained as a Red Army captain; Soviets install him as leader
Korean War invasion, Pusan Perimeter and US bombing campaign told at length
Juche ideology presented as propaganda; later Paektu birth myth for Kim Jong Il
Kim Jong Un born 1984, regime later falsified it as 1982
Long segment on his adolescence at school near Bern, Switzerland
2010 Cheonan sinking, possibly ordered by Kim Jong Un as heir
Execution of uncle Jang Song-thaek in 2013 and other purges
State hacking and the 2014 Sony attack over The Interview
Nuclear tests, ballistic missiles and the growth of the arsenal under Kim Jong Un
Summit with the US president framed as a diplomatic win for the regime

notes: Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il are secondary with long segments, so covered_span starts at Kim Il Sung's 1912 birth. main_span starts in 2010 with the Cheonan sinking and accelerated succession; Kim Jong Un was alive at release. The 1990s famine gets real time but has no matching theme. Wikidata QIDs omitted for lack of certainty.
